report.tagline: Indian-language social apps where people share posts, short videos and live streams, now earning more from live-stream gifts and paid micro-dramas than from ads.
report.simpleSummary: ShareChat is a social app for people who prefer Hindi, Tamil, Bhojpuri and other Indian languages over English. You scroll posts, Good Morning images, jokes and videos, and you can join live audio and video rooms with creators. Moj is its short video app, which grew fast after India banned TikTok in 2020. The same company, Mohalla Tech, also runs QuickTV, an app of short paid soap-opera style shows called micro-dramas.

overview.whatItDoes: ShareChat and Moj give India's non-English speakers a place to watch, share and create content in their own language. The company makes money when users buy virtual gifts for live hosts, pay for micro-drama episodes on QuickTV, or see ads. After years of heavy losses chasing Instagram, it cut costs and moved to money from users directly.
howItWorks: Users pick a language at sign-up, from about 15 Indian languages, and see a feed in that language.
ShareChat's feed mixes images, status posts, short videos and memes that people forward to WhatsApp.
Moj is a full-screen short video feed with filters and music, like Instagram Reels.
Live 'chatrooms' and live video let hosts talk with fans, who buy coins and send virtual gifts.
QuickTV sells micro-dramas: 1 to 2 minute episodes where the first few are free and later ones need coins or a subscription.
Advertisers buy video and display ads to reach small-town and rural India.
overview.valueProposition: For users: entertainment and community in your own language, made by people like you, on a cheap phone. For advertisers: reach Bharat, meaning users in smaller towns that English platforms serve less well.

painPoints.pain: Most big apps are built for English speakers, so many Indians feel left out.
painPoints.howSolved: Every screen, feed and creator is in the user's chosen Indian language.

painPoints.pain: After the TikTok ban in 2020, millions of short video fans and creators lost their app.
painPoints.howSolved: Moj launched within days and took in TikTok users and creators.

painPoints.pain: People in small towns feel lonely and want someone to talk with.
painPoints.howSolved: Live audio and video rooms let them chat with hosts and other fans in real time.

painPoints.pain: Long TV serials take hours, but people only have a few minutes at a time.
painPoints.howSolved: QuickTV micro-dramas tell a full story in 1 to 2 minute episodes.

painPoints.pain: Finding daily shareable content for WhatsApp groups takes effort.
painPoints.howSolved: ShareChat's feed is full of ready-to-share status posts, wishes and memes with a WhatsApp share button.

painPoints.pain: Brands find it hard to reach rural and small-town users in their language.
painPoints.howSolved: ShareChat and Moj ads target by language and region.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows content only in the language a user picks.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: This is the main reason users choose ShareChat over Instagram or YouTube.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Hosts run audio or video rooms; fans buy coins with UPI and send gifts.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The biggest revenue line at ₹472 crore in FY26, and it does not depend on advertisers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Full-screen vertical video feed with editing tools and music.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Keeps young users and creators on the platform and creates ad space.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Paid short episodic shows; first episodes free, then pay per episode or subscribe.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Drove most of the ₹293 crore subscription revenue and has over 5 crore Play Store downloads.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: One tap to share any post or video into WhatsApp chats and status.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Free marketing: every share carries the ShareChat watermark to new users.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Paid tiers with perks for fans and creators.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Adds steady money from users beyond one-off gifts.

userJourneys.name: First open after a WhatsApp forward

steps.detail: Gets a Hindi devotional video in a family group with a ShareChat watermark.
Downloads ShareChat from the Play Store on a ₹8,000 Android phone.
Chooses Hindi; no English typing needed.
Sees wishes, news and jokes in Hindi.
Forwards a Good Morning post to WhatsApp, bringing in the next user.

userJourneys.name: Sending a first gift in a live room

steps.detail: 'Your favourite host is live now' pops up at 9 pm.
The host greets users who send gifts by name.
Pays a small amount like ₹49 via UPI for a coin pack.
A rose or a car animation plays on screen; the host thanks him.
Returns the next night, and may climb the room's top gifter list.
A Moj or Instagram ad shows a dramatic 30-second clip.
Watches the first 8 to 10 episodes for free.
A cliffhanger, then a prompt to unlock with coins.
Buys coins or a weekly pass by UPI.

steps.step: Finishes and gets a new show
steps.detail: The app recommends a similar drama to keep her watching.

businessModel.summary: ShareChat makes money in three ways: users buy gifts for live hosts, users pay to watch micro-dramas and premium perks, and brands buy ads. In FY26, almost 75% of revenue came straight from users, a big change from its old ad-only model.

revenueStreams.detail: Users buy coins and gift them to hosts. ShareChat keeps a cut and pays the rest to hosts. ₹472 crore in FY26.
QuickTV micro-drama unlocks and passes, plus Moj+ and Moj Blue. ₹293 crore in FY26.
Video and banner ads to reach Indian-language users. ₹252 crore in FY26, down 13%.

businessModel.pricing: Free to use. Coin packs and micro-drama unlocks start at small amounts paid by UPI; exact prices change often and are shown in the app.
costDrivers: Pay-outs to live hosts and micro-drama production
Marketing to get new users and drama watchers (₹335 crore in FY26, up 7.7 times)
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough math: about ₹1,016 crore of yearly revenue across an estimated 300 million monthly users is only about ₹34 per user per year. The money comes from a small group: if around 1% to 2% of users pay, each payer brings in a few thousand rupees a year. On ₹100 of gifts, the company keeps roughly ₹30 to ₹50 after paying the host, then pays for servers and moderation. Micro-dramas earn more per payer but need heavy ad spending to find each new viewer. In April to June 2026 the business finally broke even at the EBITDA level.

howTheyGetUsers: WhatsApp forwards with a ShareChat or Moj watermark
Paid ads for QuickTV dramas on Meta, YouTube and its own apps
Pre-installs and Play Store search in Hindi and regional languages
Creators bringing their fans from other apps
whatBringsUsersBack: Daily habit of finding wishes and posts to forward
Live hosts who know regulars by name and run nightly shows
Leaderboards and badges for top gifters
growth.moat: ShareChat has years of data on what people in each Indian language and region like, plus a base of local creators and hosts. Meta and Google are strong in Indian languages too, so the moat is narrow. Its best defence is the live gifting and micro-drama business, which depends on close host relationships and local stories.

competitors.name: Instagram Reels
competitors.positioning: Meta's short video, the market leader in India after the TikTok ban.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Moj is fully language-first and pays creators through gifts, but Instagram has far more users and brand deals.

competitors.name: YouTube Shorts
competitors.positioning: Google's short video, bundled with YouTube's huge base.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: ShareChat has live rooms and a WhatsApp-forward culture; Shorts has better creator pay through YouTube.

competitors.name: Josh (VerSe Innovation)
competitors.positioning: Another Indian short video app born after the TikTok ban.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Similar product. ShareChat has moved further into live gifting and paid micro-dramas.

competitors.name: Kuku TV, Pocket FM and other micro-drama apps
competitors.positioning: Paid short episodic shows and audio series for India.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: QuickTV can promote its shows to ShareChat and Moj users for free, which cuts marketing costs.

competitors.name: Chamet, Eloelo and other live apps
competitors.positioning: Live video and audio rooms with gifting.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: ShareChat already has a big audience to move into live rooms.

northStar.metric: Weekly minutes of content watched or listened to in a user's own language, per active user
northStar.why: A north star metric should show value to users. Time spent with content in one's own language is the core value. It feeds all three revenue lines: more viewing means more ad space, more gifting and more drama unlocks.

guardrailMetrics: Share of harmful or adult content reported in live rooms
Uninstall rate after the first paywall

strengths: Deep understanding of Indian-language users in small towns
Live gifting and paid dramas make it less dependent on ads
First EBITDA profitable quarter in mid-2026 after deep cost cuts
Can promote its own micro-drama app to a large base for free
weaknesses: Revenue per user is very low compared with global social apps
Heavy reliance on a small group of big spenders in live rooms
Large non-cash losses and a history of layoffs hurt its brand with investors and staff
risks: Instagram and YouTube keep improving Indian-language support
Rules on online gaming, gifting or ads could change, as the 2025 gaming ban did
Micro-drama market is crowded and marketing costs are rising
Weak stock markets could delay the planned 2027 IPO
userComplaints: Live hosts pressure users to send gifts
Micro-dramas lock episodes behind payment right at the cliffhanger
Low-quality, repeated or misleading content in the feed
Account bans or lost coins with slow support

improvementIdeas.idea: Monthly spend limits and a weekly spend summary for coin buyers.
improvementIdeas.problem: Users complain about overspending in live rooms, which is also a regulatory risk.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More trust and fewer refund requests, protecting long-term gifting.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of payers still paying after 3 months

improvementIdeas.idea: Cross-promote QuickTV inside Moj with the first episode played right in the feed.
improvementIdeas.problem: Micro-drama marketing spend rose 7.7 times; buying users from Meta is costly.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lower cost to get each new paying viewer.

improvementIdeas.idea: Season pass for a full drama at a fixed price shown upfront.
improvementIdeas.problem: Users dislike surprise paywalls and per-episode costs adding up.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher conversion and fewer angry reviews.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Free-to-paid conversion and Play Store rating

improvementIdeas.idea: Creator earnings dashboard in Moj with brand-deal matching for regional creators.
improvementIdeas.problem: Creators leave for Instagram where brand money is.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More fresh content and lower creator churn.

improvementIdeas.idea: Lite mode for phones under 3GB of RAM with fewer ads per session.
improvementIdeas.problem: Many target users have budget phones and slow data.

pmLessons: Language can be a product, but not a moat by itself. Once Meta and Google added Indian languages, ShareChat had to find a new edge.
Ads in small towns pay little, so many Indian consumer apps earn more by letting users pay small amounts directly through UPI.
Profit can matter more than growth. ShareChat cut costs and shifted focus to reach its first profitable quarter.
Look at where losses come from. Its ₹1,978 crore FY26 loss was mostly non-cash, while the real cash loss was ₹91 crore.

interviewQuestions.question: ShareChat's ad revenue fell while live-stream revenue grew. How should it split its product investment?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue per user, growth and risk of each line. Talk about dependency on a few big spenders. Suggest a portfolio with clear metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase gifting in live rooms without hurting users?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users by spend. Find levers: host quality, social recognition, small first packs. Add guardrails like spend limits and complaint rates.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you compete with Instagram Reels in Tier 2 and 3 towns?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a niche where ShareChat can win: language, live interaction, local creators. Avoid head-on fights on generic short video.

interviewQuestions.question: Design the paywall for a micro-drama app.
interviewQuestions.hint: Define where to place it, free episode count, pricing (per episode vs pass), and A/B testing. Track conversion, completion and ratings.

interviewQuestions.question: What metrics would you show investors before an IPO?
interviewQuestions.hint: Revenue growth, share from users vs ads, EBITDA trend, paying users, retention, and cost to acquire a payer. Explain why each matters.
